thesis: Held, at the lowest conviction I have written, and for a reason I want on the record: none of the conditions I named to kill this have actually fired. Brent surged 9% on the week to about $104, the stop at 62.85 is far below the 65.14 close, and the divergence test I set on 10 September needs a full week - it has been two days. But Gulf diplomats meet Iran on Monday about a temporary Hormuz shipping arrangement, which is the event I said would invalidate this immediately, and I cannot handicap it.
bull_case:
Pattern analyst: setup is a **failed breakout so far** - XLE made its 55-day and near-52-week high at 65.735 on 9 September and has not exceeded it in three sessions, closing 65.14, just 0.3% below the 252-day high with RSI 60 and 63d momentum +14.9%. It is not extended by the test (RSI 60, well under 70). Squeeze is 0.83, so no coil; ATR 1.9% keeps the stop manageable. The rs column is empty, but momentum +14.9% against SPY's +3.9% is derivable and says XLE leads the US benchmark by about 11 points - it is not a laggard. Verdict: pattern says wait for a close above 65.74 before adding.

The commodity is doing the work: Brent settled near $104 on Friday, up 9% on the week, after US-Iran tit-for-tat strikes. Goldman warns Brent could exceed $120 in 2027 if Gulf output stays 4 mb/d below prewar levels, and the EIA has *raised* its 2H26 Brent forecast to about $90/b. Exxon and Chevron are 42.5% of the fund with Chevron committing $7B to double Venezuelan output, and the sector's headline tone in today's packet is +0.67, the joint highest in the book.
bear_case:
The scheduled risk is Monday. Iranian state media say Tehran will meet Gulf states in Oman, and GCC diplomats meet their Iranian counterpart on Monday to discuss a temporary arrangement for managing shipping through the Strait - Brent already paused its rally on that news. Both prior XLE memos said a reopening of Hormuz transits invalidates this immediately regardless of price. Talks are not a reopening, but this is the event, and it is two days away with the position fully invested and no cash to respond.

The demand side has turned openly bearish: the IEA sharply cut its global demand outlook, forecasting a 2.5 mb/d contraction in 2026, and the EIA raised its 2027 US crude production forecast to 14.3 mb/d. Goldman's December 2026 Brent forecast is $85 - about 18% below spot. And the vehicle question is still open: Brent rose 9% on the week while XLE fell 0.9% and DBC gained; the equities are not translating the commodity. That test needs until 17 September before it counts, and I am not calling it early. Desk record check (research/outcomes.json): 9 closed trades, 0 wins, -$97.25 realised, expectancy -2.08% per trade; long memos are 2 good out of 4 judged, a coin flip. Conviction here is set stingier than the evidence alone would suggest, because the evidence alone has not yet earned better.
catalysts: Monday's GCC-Iran meeting in Oman on a temporary Hormuz shipping arrangement
15-16 Sep 2026 FOMC and the demand outlook
Whether XLE can close above its 65.74 high
Q3 oil-major earnings in late October
risks: Monday's Hormuz talks: the named immediate invalidation, two days out
IEA forecasts a 2.5 mb/d demand contraction in 2026
EIA raised 2027 US production to 14.3 mb/d; Goldman sees Brent $85 in December
Brent +9% on the week while XLE fell 0.9%: the equities are not following
No cash left to react - the book is fully invested
Desk record: long memos 2-for-4, nine of nine closed trades lost
invalidation: The pattern analyst's level is **62.85**, the trailing stop shown in the packet, and it binds before my 62.00 thesis level from 9 September. A daily close below 62.85 ends this. Separately and unchanged: a confirmed reopening of Hormuz transits or a US-Iran ceasefire invalidates it immediately regardless of price, and if XLE is still lagging a rising Brent on 17 September the vehicle choice was wrong and this goes flat then.
